images.title: Two friends, two heights
images.purpose: Set the opening scene: two adult friends of different heights standing against a height scale, inviting a guess from experience.
images.composition: Two flat, faceless adult figures stand side by side in the centre against a tall wall height scale on the left, with wide white space around them.
exact_structure: A vertical grey (#6B7280) height scale on the left edge with two marks: a short horizontal teal (#0072B2) line labelled 5 feet and, higher up the scale, a short horizontal amber (#E69F00) line labelled 6 feet; the two heights drawn to scale (5 to 6).

Exactly 2 standing adult figures, flat style, no faces, no hair or clothing details that show gender: the left figure in teal (#0072B2) is exactly as tall as the 5 feet line, the right figure in amber (#E69F00) is exactly as tall as the 6 feet line.
A thin dashed teal line runs from the top of the left figure to the 5 feet mark; a thin dashed amber line runs from the top of the right figure to the 6 feet mark.
A single reddish purple (#CC79A7) question mark floats above and between the two figures.
Nothing else in the frame: no background scenery, no other people.
rejection: the shorter figure not lining up with 5 feet, or the taller not lining up with 6 feet
faces, clothing or hairstyles that state a gender
any written guess or caption naming a man or a woman
images.takeaway: A guess based on many people we have seen before is a first step in statistical thinking.
images.description: Two plain flat figures, one 5 feet tall in teal and one 6 feet tall in amber, stand beside a height scale with a purple question mark above them.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Ask students to make their guess before reading on and to say what past experience the guess comes from.

image_decisions.why: The hook needs a simple scene of the two heights so students form a guess before the reasoning.
